title: Stop reading the changelog out loud
one_sentence_promise: A four-minute two-host brief beats a forty-minute recap when every beat carries one idea and the voices actually sound like people.

beats.purpose: Hook: the standup that became a recap
beats.one_idea: Nobody wants the changelog read to them.
Four minutes, two hosts, one product decision.
Heavy model writes, a judge scores, speech tags carry emotion.
If they cannot repeat one sentence, you failed.

cold_open_candidates.text: The entire standup was a forty-minute recap of a changelog nobody would read.
We measured it. Twelve people, zero could quote the launch.
I used to ship those recaps. I thought thorough meant kind.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: So I walked in and the entire standup was a forty-minute recap of a changelog nobody would read.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: We've all been in that room. Someone is still sharing the Jira board.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Today we cut one product to four minutes. No mush.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: Impact Brief is a two-host product podcast. Not a newsletter with a mouth. Not a model summarizing docs in a calm voice until you forget why you pressed play.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The constraint is four to six minutes, not forty. If a decision cannot survive that, it was never a decision. It was a tour.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: One sentence the listener can steal. That's the whole product requirement.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How it is made, because this is the part people get wrong. A heavy generative model writes the outline and the performance. It is allowed to be bold. It is not allowed to be the judge of its own cleverness.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: The judge is Jev. Typed decisions only. Choice, noul, score. Probabilities, not paragraphs. If a beat is mush, code sends it back. The writer does not grade itself.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Then the voices. xAI speech, leo and ara in this show. Laughs, pauses, emphasis live in the text. That is not decoration. That is the difference between a briefing and a hostage situation.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: Sound effects are optional punctuation. One hit on the open if you must. One ding on a number that actually matters. Maybe a whoosh between sections. No bed humming under the argument like a spa.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If the hosts need a laugh, they laugh. We do not mix in a sitcom track. I will die on that hill and it is a very small hill.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: Here is the only metric I will defend. After the close, can they repeat the promise. We tested twelve teammates on a forty-minute recap. Zero quoted the launch. Zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We cut the same launch to five minutes, two hosts, one idea per beat. Nine of twelve said the sentence back. Same facts. Different spine.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: That is not a lab coat study. It is a room full of tired people. Treat it as a dare, not a paper.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If your brief needs a graph to be interesting, you buried the lede in the axis labels.

turns.speaker: ara
turns.text: Steal the format. Clone the kit. Bring your own preset if your show is comedy, or a course, or a story that is allowed to cry. This example is a product brief. It is not the whole studio.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ship a brief people finish. That is the job. We will see you on the next one, and it will not be forty minutes.
